title: Sparsity-adaptive attention kernel multiplexing across MIG slices
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem: For mixed-MIG GPU hosts we observe suboptimal tail latency when running attention-heavy workloads with varying sparsity (e.g., instruction- and code-completion prompts vs chat). Current kernel selector picks a single best dense attention kernel per model shape, which performs poorly when token-level sparsity causes execution characteristics to flip between favoring block-sparse vs dense kernels. This is exacerbated when MIG slices have heterogeneous clock/power states and memory bandwidth, causing one slice to be better for sparse kernels while another prefers dense kernels.

Goal: Implement a runtime layer that can multiplex between candidate attention kernels per-request based on a lightweight sparsity and bandwidth probe, and route execution fragments to the best MIG slice/kernel combo while minimizing additional scheduling latency and preserving KV-cache correctness across fragments.
design_notes:
- Add a per-request sparsity estimator that samples attention masks during the prefill (priming) phase; estimator must be O(1) relative to token length (fixed-size sample).
- Extend the kernel catalog metadata with sparsity-performance curves (sparsity fraction -> estimated tokens/sec) per SKU and per MIG partition class.
- Implement a short speculative execution path: for the first decode step after prefill, run a tiny probe micro-batch (1-2 tokens) on the top-2 kernel candidates concurrently on different MIG slices if capacity permits; use observed per-token latency to finalize kernel selection for the remaining sequence.
- Ensure KV-cache immutability: when fragmenting work across slices/kernels, use logical sequence IDs and a deterministic merge step that only touches metadata pointers to avoid copying KV tensors.
- Fallback policy: if probing increases latency beyond a threshold (empirically 5% of budget), revert to historical best kernel for the route.
- Telemetry: record probe outcomes, chosen kernel, slice affinity, and end-to-end latency to populate telemetry tables and update the kernel-sparsity curves automatically.
experiments: Microbench: run synthetic sparsity grid (0%->90% random mask) for 6 model shapes on H100 L40S and A10 across 3 MIG partition sizes
On-host perf: Canary workloads on dedicated dev cluster with mixed-tenant traffic to measure tail P95/P99 change
Integration: End-to-end run with real customer prompt mix (anonymized) to validate quality regression and latency impact
metrics: primary: P95 latency (ms) for attention-heavy routes
probe-overhead: fraction of requests where probe added >2ms
cost-est: delta GPU-utilization and per-token cost estimate
rollout_plan: 1) Lab: implement estimator + kernel metadata and run offline microbench (2 weeks)
2) Canary: enable speculative probe on 5% of traffic on a dedicated MIG-fleet (4 weeks)
3) Gradual ramp: roll to 25%/50%/100% with automatic rollback on quality/latency regressions
4) Release: enable metadata-driven automatic tuning + dashboard surface for customers
risks: KV-cache merge bugs could cause subtle state corruption across fragments
Probing on critical low-latency routes could increase tail latency if not appropriately throttled
Telemetry skew due to cold MLC caches on certain SKUs leading to miscalibrated curves
acceptance_criteria: No KV-cache regressions across 50k end-to-end test traces
P95 latency improvement of >=10% for mixed-sparsity workloads in canary compared to baseline
Probe overhead < 2% of total requests and <5% of per-request latency budget
Added telemetry populates kernel-sparsity curves and shows sensible monotonicity
